title: iOS 7 interface
lede: Apple’s 2013 redesign that dropped the textures of earlier iOS for flatter icons and thinner type.
summary: Flatter icons, slimmer fonts, and redesigned apps in Apple’s mobile system. Jony Ive’s team, 2013.

creator.name: Apple (design team led by Jony Ive)

evidence.note: Wikipedia article read on 2026-09-28. The home screen is visible only small and at an angle in the capture of [Apple’s iOS 7 page](ref:apple-ios-7-website-2013), so the record is not marked observed.

styles.note: The turn of the most skeuomorphic mobile system to flat design; partial fit, because the icons keep soft gradients and the system uses translucent blurred panels.

context: iOS 7 was announced on 10 June 2013 and released on 18 September 2013. It “introduced a completely redesigned user interface, a design credited to a team led by Apple’s former senior vice president of design, Jony Ive” ([Wikipedia: iOS 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOS_7)).
Wikipedia quotes the redesign as “sharper, flatter icons, slimmer fonts, a new slide-to-unlock function, and a new control panel that slides up from the bottom of the screen”.
Ive: “There is a profound and enduring beauty in simplicity, in clarity, in efficiency.”
Wikipedia’s article on [Letterpress](ref:letterpress-app-2012) states that Ive took inspiration from minimalist iOS apps, among them Letterpress, for the iOS 7 graphics.
interpretation: The style record lists Helvetica Neue as the iOS 7 face and treats iOS 7 as part of the flat turn. Its blurred panels also point toward [glassmorphism](style:glassmorphism).

rights.statement: Apple software; copyrighted. No image is stored here.
